suppress.reason: The review skill quotes src/auth.ts:88 inside an example of a well-written review sentence. It is deliberately not a real path here, and resolving it would be meaningless — the same case as the illustrative citation already suppressed under docs/references/.
A changelog describes past releases. Citing code as it was at release time is correct, not rot.
The reference guides use src/ai/brain.ts:301 as an illustrative citation example. It is deliberately not a real path in this repository, and resolving it would be meaningless.

A fragment, not a standalone document: the homepage renders it beneath its own <h1>, so a heading here would be a second top-level title on that page. It is the one file in the corpus written to be included rather than read on its own.
The README opens with a block-art banner spelling the project name, which is the title. GitHub renders the repository name above it, so an H1 would be a third copy of the same word.
GitHub renders a pull-request template as the body of a new PR, where an H1 would become a stray heading in every description. It is a form, not a document.
